lines.text: How long to walk to the Moon? Starting at your own front door.
lines.phonemes: hˌaʊ lˈɔŋ tə wˈɔːk tə ðə mˈuːn? stˈɑːɹɾɪŋ æt jʊɹ ˈoʊn fɹˈʌnt dˈɔːɹ.

lines.text: The Moon sits about thirty Earths away, lined up side by side, with nothing but dark between. That is a very long way for a pair of shoes.
lines.phonemes: ðə mˈuːn sˈɪts ɐbˌaʊt θˈɜːɾi ˈɜːθs ɐwˈeɪ, lˈaɪnd ˌʌp sˈaɪd baɪ sˈaɪd, wɪð nˈʌθɪŋ bˌʌt dˈɑːɹk bᵻtwˈiːn. ðæt ɪz ɐ vˈɛɹi lˈɔŋ wˈeɪ fɚɹə pˈɛɹ ʌv ʃˈuːz.

lines.text: Walk at an easy pace, the kind you could chat through. Never stop, not even to sleep. You would arrive in about nine years.
lines.phonemes: wˈɔːk æɾ ɐn ˈiːzi pˈeɪs, ðə kˈaɪnd juː kʊd tʃˈæt θɹˈuː. nˈɛvɚ stˈɑːp, nˌɑːt ˈiːvən tə slˈiːp. juː wʊd ɚɹˈaɪv ɪn ɐbˌaʊt nˈaɪn jˈɪɹz.

lines.text: But nobody walks day and night. You sleep, you eat, you stop to tie a shoe. So give yourself a working day of walking.
lines.phonemes: bˌʌt nˈoʊbɑːdi wˈɔːks dˈeɪ ænd nˈaɪt. juː slˈiːp, juː ˈiːt, juː stˈɑːp tə tˈaɪ ɐ ʃˈuː. sˌoʊ ɡˈɪv jɔːɹsˈɛlf ɐ wˈɜːkɪŋ dˈeɪ ʌv wˈɔːkɪŋ.

lines.text: A working day of walking gets you there in about twenty-six years. Stick to the popular daily step goal, and it is closer to a hundred and forty.
lines.phonemes: ɐ wˈɜːkɪŋ dˈeɪ ʌv wˈɔːkɪŋ ɡˈɛts juː ðɛɹ ɪn ɐbˌaʊt twˈɛntisˈɪks jˈɪɹz. stˈɪk tə ðə pˈɑːpjʊlɚ dˈeɪli stˈɛp ɡˈoʊl, ænd ɪɾ ɪz klˈoʊsɚ tʊ ɐ hˈʌndɹɪd ænd fˈɔːɹɾi.

lines.text: Slower adds years, quicker trims a few, but it never gets close.
lines.phonemes: slˈoʊɚɹ ˈædz jˈɪɹz, kwˈɪkɚ tɹˈɪmz ɐ fjˈuː, bˌʌt ɪt nˈɛvɚ ɡˈɛts klˈoʊs.

lines.text: The Apollo crews made the same trip in about three days. The distance never changed, only the speed.
lines.phonemes: ðɪ ɐpˈɑːloʊ kɹˈuːz mˌeɪd ðə sˈeɪm tɹˈɪp ɪn ɐbˌaʊt θɹˈiː dˈeɪz. ðə dˈɪstəns nˈɛvɚ tʃˈeɪndʒd, ˈoʊnli ðə spˈiːd.

lines.text: Next envelope: what if everyone on Earth held hands?
